title: Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers — Reinstated Term and New Expiry Date
content:
**Para. 1.** Reinstating an expired credit of Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers gives it a new term of validity, the reinstated term, counted in whole calendar months.

**Para. 2.** The reinstated term is the instrument's reinstated validity months.

**Para. 3.** A reinstated term never exceeds 12 calendar months, and this cap is the final step in working out the term. The cap acts on the figure the term comes to once every month counted toward it has been added together and every treatment of those months has been applied. Nothing further is done to the term after it is capped. A term that comes to more than 12 months at that point is 12.

**Para. 4.** The new expiry date is the reinstatement date plus the reinstated term in calendar months. Adding the months keeps the day of the month, and falls back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist.

## Reading the paragraphs together

| Input | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Reinstated term | the instrument's reinstated validity months, never above 12, the cap applied last |
| Reinstatement date | the date on which the credit is reinstated |
| New expiry date | reinstatement date plus the reinstated term, same day of the month, or the month's last day where that day does not exist |

## Worked examples (hypothetical instrument whose reinstated validity months are 6)

- *Ordinary date.* A credit reinstated on 15 January 2026 has a reinstated term of 6 months, and its new expiry date is 15 July 2026.
- *Month-end fallback.* A credit reinstated on 31 August 2026 has a reinstated term of 6 months. 31 February does not exist, so the new expiry date is 28 February 2027, the last day of that month.
- *Leap year.* A credit reinstated on 31 August 2027 has a new expiry date of 29 February 2028, because February 2028 has 29 days.

## Cap illustrated (hypothetical)

| Term as worked out, before the final cap (months) | Reinstated term after the cap (months) |
|---|---|
| 6 | 6 |
| 12 | 12 |
| 14 | 12 |
